newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products- Gulf prices dive on stock data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products- Gulf prices dive on stock data.

text.p: U.S. Gulf and New York Harbor product prices fell sharply in early Wednesday action on weaker differentials and basis prices, pressured by the data showing extremely high production levels in the latest week.
However, some differentials in the Midcontinent firmed as continued pipeline delays forced players to bid up prompt supplies, traders said.
On the NYMEX, June gasoline futures fell sharply, shedding 1.26 cents, while June heating oil dropped 0.53 cent.
The American Petroleum Institute data released Tuesday showed a build in gasoline stocks of 6.5 million barrels, well above market expectations, with daily refinery output of 8.1 million barrels.
++ GASOLINE: Conventional M2 gasoline differentials slipped lower, with prompt barrels offered at about 1.80 cents under the June futures, according to traders.
However, prompt reformulated A2 gasoline remained on offer at 1.50 cents over the June futures, steady with late Tuesday levels.

++ DISTILLATE: Market players quoted prompt heating oil barrels at slighlty under the June NYMEX market, though low sulphur diesel weakened about 0.50 cent, with prompt barrels offered at 0.75 cent over the June futures.
++ GASOLINE: Differentials also weakened as buyers backed out of the market, putting prompt conventional M1 between about 3.60 and 3.85 cents under the screen, down about 0.25 cent from Tuesday.

++ DISTILLATE: Amples supplies drove differentials lower, with prompt heating oil talked near 2.50 cents under the June NYMEX, and prompt low sulphur diesel talked at 1.85 cents off the June NYMEX, both about 0.50 cent below Tuesday's levels.
"There's a lot of oil down here," said one trader, referring to the softer distillate values.

++ GASOLINE: Prompt Group Three unleaded differentials rose a half cent to between 5.25 cents and 5.50 cents over NYMEX June gasoline as continued delays on the Explorer Pipeline put pressure on the front end in the Midwest. Traders said a 5.50 cent deal over the screen was done this morning for delivery by Thursday.
Shipments on the 14th cycle have been delayed by about five to ten days on the Explorer pipeline. The delay means less material was being stored in the Williams System, which feeds the Midwest.
"There are a couple of sellers who have unleaded in the Williams pipeline system and can deliver the barrels now," said a Houston trader.
Chicago unleaded differentials were steady at 2.75 cents amid the sharp decline on NYMEX June gasoline futures.
Group Three premium differentials traded at 3.25 cents over the screen, about a quarter cent stronger from Wednesday. Chicago material differentials held steady.
